question: Human footprints at White Sands, New Mexico, could change when people first reached the Americas. How old are they?
answer: About 21,000 to 23,000 years, from the depth of the last ice age, thousands of years before people were long thought to have arrived. The first dates rested on one material with a known flaw. Two unrelated methods, with different weaknesses, landing on the same answer is what settled it.
move: One method can be fooled; two unrelated methods rarely fail the same way.
ask: What do I believe that rests on one source I never questioned?

clues.text: The human prints cross tracks of mammoths, gone for over 10,000 years.
Seeds of a pond plant in the layers radiocarbon-date to 21,000-23,000 years.
Pond plants soak up old carbon from groundwater, so they can look too old.
Pollen of land conifers, which take carbon from the air, gives the same age.
Quartz grains, dated by when they last saw sunlight, agree too.

scene.why: The seeds alone could not decide. Pollen that took its carbon from air gave the same 22,000 years.

reference: Pigati et al., Independent age estimates resolve the controversy of ancient human footprints at White Sands, Science, 2023
